text:
Ravi: Heads up — we've had recurring p95/p99 SLO misses on /generate in us-west-2 since ~03:00 UTC. Spike correlates with long max-batches and queue depth rising.
Linh: Any recent config pushes to that pool?
Ravi: Yeah pushed a default bump to max_batch_size for a model family yesterday to improve throughput. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/queue-depth?orgId=1&var-pool=us-west-2-gpu-pool-3
Ravi: Config snippet:
```
model-serving:
  max_batch_size: 64
  batch_window_ms: 16
admission:
  qos_target:
    p50_ms: 80
    p95_ms: 300
```
InfraBot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for route /generate (p95=360ms > 300ms) — impacted pool: us-west-2-gpu-pool-3
Ashley: This smells like packing limit + continuous-batching pressure. When many short requests hit, the runtime packs up to 64 -> big KV-cache churn + longer decode bursts -> long tail.
Mike: If we drop max_batch_size we should expect higher per-token GPU inefficiency (cost up) but lower tail latency. Tradeoff question: customer-visible SLO vs unit cost.
Linh: Also see admission backlog queue climbing to 120 requests — admission controller backs off but allows big batches, so scheduling delay spikes.
Ravi: Proposed mitigation:
- roll max_batch_size -> 32 on pool us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%)
- reduce batch_window_ms -> 8ms for short-request-heavy models
- add a per-model qps cap for the noisy model
Command to run (canary):
```
redwoodctl deploy-config --pool us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 \
  --set model-serving.max_batch_size=32 \
  --set model-serving.batch_window_ms=8 \
  --canary 0.05
```
Ashley: Also recommend enabling "pack-priority": prefer smaller batches when queue depth is high. There's a runtime flag we can flip per-pool.
Mike: We should weigh cost: estimate says ~12% higher tokens/sec cost at steady-state with lower packing, but p95 improves by ~45%. I prefer SLOs here.
Linh: Any region constraints? This is isolated to us-west-2 pool 3 where utilization has been ~78% last 36h.
Ravi: Correct — other pools unaffected. Capacity headroom low because of rush from new dedicated customers.
Ashley: Starting canary now at 03:24, 5% traffic. I'll monitor latency and KV-cache miss rate.
InfraBot: NOTE: Deploy job queued: deploy-cfg-1772001133-canary (owner: Ashley)
Mike: If canary drops throughput too much we can also enable selective quantization fallback for long-context requests to reduce decode CPU.
Linh: Good call — also add short-term guard: cap max inflight per-connection to prevent one client from filling a batch.
Ashley: Canary results after 30m: p95 dropped from 360ms -> 180ms, queue depth and admission backlog both improved. KV-cache miss rate down.
Ravi: Nice. Roll to 25% now, then full if stable.
Ashley: Rolling to 25%.
Mike: Please add a follow-up action in infra board: evaluate automated detection for packing-induced tail latency and automated rollback thresholds.
Linh: Filing infra task: INFRA-7421 "Detect & mitigate packing-induced tail latency" — includes runbook and cost-impact analysis.
Ashley: Will post a short postmortem if anything unexpected. For now metrics look good. :thumbsup:
Ravi: Thanks all — close loop after full rollout and put this in next week's capacity planning meeting.
